summary: Keepalive pool shrink combined with GPU thermal reset causes sustained 5xx spike for streaming-heavy tenant
description:
Issue summary:
Customer observed a sustained increase in 502/503/504 rates beginning 2026-03-10 02:10 UTC that correlated with an unusually high number of long-lived streaming sessions from a single tenant. Impact: several production endpoints returned intermittent 5xx responses and streaming sessions dropped.

Impact:
- Affected customer reported 30-60% request failure rate for streaming route /v1/chat/stream for ~45 minutes.
- Customer-facing latency grew from median 80ms to 600ms before failures.
- Billing-sensitive calls (short sync chat) also saw elevated 5xx floor.

Environment:
- prod-us-east
- Customer tier: dedicated
- Affected models: ["redwood/opt-6.7b-q4", "open/llama2-13b-quant"]
- Components: ["api-gateway", "serving-runtime", "keepalive-proxy", "gpu-driver"]

Timeline & Steps to reproduce:
1) 2026-03-10 02:08 UTC: Customer ramps long-lived streaming sessions (many simultaneous small-heartbeat streams, 10-30s ping interval).
2) 02:10 UTC: apigw keepalive pool utilization climbed to 98% (accept queues increased).
3) 02:12 UTC: several runtime workers logged GPU thermal throttling and subsequent NVIDIA driver resets on nodes hosting the customer's dedicated pool.
4) 02:14-02:50 UTC: API gateway returned a mix of 502/503/504; streaming sessions reported half-open sockets and heartbeats dropped.
5) After 02:50 UTC: autoscaler and kube-level restarts reduced concurrency and error rate slowly returned to baseline.

Observed logs / metric excerpts:
- apigw.keepalive_pool.active: 3125 (pool capacity 3200)
- apigw.accept_queue.length: spiked from 12 -> 490 in 3m
- runtime.gpu.thermal.throttle_events: 7 events across 4 nodes within 5m
- runtime.driver.reset_count: 4 per affected node
- svc.streaming.session_drops: +4200 in 30m window
- sample runtime log lines:
  [2026-03-10T02:12:07Z] runtime: gpu0 thermal threshold reached, frequency drop
  [2026-03-10T02:12:09Z] runtime: nvml: driver reset invoked (errno=EIO)
  [2026-03-10T02:12:12Z] proxy: upstream connection reset by peer while streaming

Hypothesis & investigation summary:
- Root cause appears to be a combination of three factors: (1) aggressive tenant-driven long-lived streaming sessions causing keepalive pool saturation in api-gateway, (2) amplified backpressure to serving runtime leading to high sustained GPU utilization in a small set of nodes, and (3) GPU thermal events triggering driver resets which cause upstream runtimes to exit and return 502/503 until recoveries occur.
- Keepalive pool shrink behavior: healthcheck/keepalive reaper aggressively reclaimed idle connections during the spike, which resulted in churn and additional connection setup under load causing accept-queue growth and proxy head-of-line blocking.
- Hedged retry behavior on client SDK increased inflight attempts, amplifying load when upstream latency climbed.

Immediate mitigations applied:
- 02:20 UTC: Support engaged SRE to temporarily increase apigw keepalive pool soft limit for affected capacity group and relax reaper aggressiveness (applied via config rollout).
- 02:26 UTC: SRE applied an autoscale policy tweak to broaden node diversity for the tenant pool (rebalanced to avoid packing on thermally-hot hosts).
- 02:30 UTC: Temporary rate cap applied on streaming route for tenant to limit new session starts (500 concurrent sessions throttle).

Follow-up actions / next steps:
- Engineering (serving-runtime) to instrument per-GPU thermal telemetry more granularly and add early-shed policy if sustained thermal throttling detected.
- API gateway team to audit keepalive reaper heuristics and add a soft-failback to avoid aggressive reclaim under stream-heavy workloads.
- Product -> Customer Success: recommend SDK guidance for backoff/hedging on long-lived streams and provide suggested heartbeat interval (>= 60s) for heavy multiplexing clients.
- SRE runbook update: include GPU-thermal + keepalive pool interplay as a trigger for automated mitigation (temporary throttle + node reshuffle).

References:
- Grafana dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.prod/d/streams/keepalive-accept-queue?orgId=1&from=1678432800000&to=1678436400000
- Incident slack: #incidents (thread ts: 1678432920.000200)
comments: 2026-03-10 02:18 UTC - Support (Aisha Kumar): Customer opened with error traces and example request IDs; initial triage shows apigw spike. Escalating to SRE.
2026-03-10 02:25 UTC - SRE (Diego Martinez): Increased keepalive soft limit and adjusted reaper settings for the tenant pool; monitoring for error rate change.
2026-03-10 02:33 UTC - SRE (Diego Martinez): Detected GPU driver resets on nodes downstream (node-id: n-us-east-7, n-us-east-9). Applying temporary node drain and reshuffle.
2026-03-10 02:40 UTC - Customer (Silverline AI - K. O'Neill): Confirmed reduced session drops after mitigation but still seeing occasional 502s on very hot flows.
2026-03-11 09:05 UTC - Runtime Eng (Lina Perez): Added instrumentation ticket and draft PR to gate session-accept behavior when thermal events are rising. See PR #4567.
2026-03-11 14:30 UTC - Product (Maya Chen): Customer success outreach planned; advise SDK changes and coordination for a scheduled config change window.
investigation_notes: SRE reproduced a correlation locally by spinning up hundreds of multiplexed streaming sessions with 15s heartbeats. With an artificially reduced keepalive pool, accept queue grew and proxied connections stalled, which pushed sustained GPU occupancy (p99 token throughput) on a small node subset and triggered thermal throttling under stress test. Hedged client retries amplified the spike. The interplay is consistent and repeatable in staging with similar constraints.
resolution: Mitigations applied reduced error rate to baseline by 02:55 UTC: increased keepalive limits, adjusted reaper, applied transient streaming throttle to tenant, and reshuffled workload off thermally-hot GPU nodes. Long-term: engineering to add early-shed on thermal telemetry and API gateway to adjust reaper heuristics. Customer will be provided SDK guidance and recommended heartbeat interval.
